dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: This is the Qiaoying Village tea workshop. Most of the tea leaves are sent here after being picked.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: You might not realize that tea leaves require several processes and careful handling before they can be used to make tea.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Simply put, we need to remove the excess moisture in the leaves to deepen their fragrance and make them easier to store.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Our workshop's in charge of sunning, baking, and then stirring them in a pan.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: Some types are then taken back by the tea farmers for additional processing, such as piling and fermenting.

dialogues.speaker: Ding Sr.
dialogues.text: If you have time, you should stay in the village for a month or so. That way, you can see the full process, from leaf picking to the moment the tea's served up on tables.
